HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Meta.Meta__Description: Quilt insulation in section - the looping batt line every drawing uses for mineral wool, running across the tile and joining the next. One run of loops to a tile, with clear paper above and below it.
HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so the hatch measures the same on the sheet at 1:20 and at 1:100. Pattern scale adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Meta.Meta__WhySeams: The run crosses the left and right seams at the TOP of a loop, where it is travelling dead level, so it meets the seam square on and the join cannot show. It keeps 2 mm clear of the top and bottom edges. Na__LeHatch__SeamCopies paints what the next tile pushes across.
HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Meta.Meta__Fitting: A run is 8 mm deep in a 12 mm tile. To fill a 100 mm quilt at 1:20 (5 mm on paper) set Pattern scale to about 0.6; at 1:50 (2 mm) about 0.25.

HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the pattern lists.
HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Identity.Identity__Note: Mineral wool and other soft insulation. Turn it with Pattern deg to run along a rafter or up a stud wall.

HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Tile.Tile__Note: One full loop down and up again. Narrow and tall, because the loops are.

HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with until a use sets its own. The stroke is 0.25 pt (0.0882 mm) at scale 1 and grows with the pattern scale; a line weight typed in the panel does not. 'inherit' takes the colour of whatever carries the hatch - a vector's edge colour - until a pattern colour is picked.

HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's own origin, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres. Strokes only: the PDF stamps a tile as lines and never fills one.

Loops.Glyph__Note: Drawn as two cubic curves - M0,2 C2.6,2 0.4,10 3,10 S3.4,2 6,2 - whose control points overshoot, which is what fattens each loop into the batt shape instead of a sine wave; level at both ends and at the middle. WRITTEN as six, each of the two cut in three, because the PDF flattens every cubic to twelve chords: two cubics made a loop of visibly straight sides on paper, six do not. The screen draws the same curve either way.

HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Placement.Place__Note: The whole tile is one glyph at the origin

HatchPattern__InsulationQuilt__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a use may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as the material.
